page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU configuration consists of 12 physical cores with a single thread per core on a shared allocation model. Memory resources include 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding 10.67 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 24 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and gzip compression tests placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average range. Memory performance is strong for large-block uncached read operations, reaching 254.5 GB/sec, while cached read and write operations remain average. For AI workloads, the NVIDIA L4 GPU achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 345.71 tokens per second on a small 135M LLM, though prompt processing speeds are average.

This server offers a specialized hardware profile that balances high-capacity system memory with dedicated GPU acceleration. The absence of bundled local storage requires external storage attachments, which is a key architectural tradeoff. Given the combination of an NVIDIA L4 GPU, 128 GB of RAM, and top-tier single-core CPU performance, this configuration is suited for light LLM inference, machine learning model prototyping, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated rendering workloads.
